reasons: Tabular timers and fixed-format decimal amounts pass across the sampled axis grid; use explicit tnum, suitable weights, and resolve locale-space/identifier requirements.
Sampled numeric/currency headings at 28–32 raster pixels are coherent across the tested weights; scoped to these data headings.
Short labels and numeric content are readable in the 400–500 native samples; locale coverage and alphanumeric ambiguity remain conditional.
No long-form reading task or user study performed; a numerical proof does not validate sustained reading.

findings.title: Locale grouping-space coverage is incomplete
findings.evidence: Actual TTF cmap contains U+00A0 but lacks U+202F narrow no-break space and U+2009 thin space. Numeric locale strings using these characters require fallback; the tested ordinary U+0020 grouping works.
findings.recommendation: Add U+202F and U+2009 with deliberate numeric grouping advances, or explicitly document and test fallback behavior for supported locales.
findings.acceptance_test: Shape 1\u202f234,56 € and 1\u2009234.56 with actual TTF and WOFF2; require no .notdef and verify stable grouping under tnum at wght 100/400/900 and opsz 9/14/128.

findings.title: Alphanumeric zero remains close to capital O
findings.evidence: Inspected native 12/14/16px O0 samples show similar unmarked oval forms, particularly at 12px; GSUB feature tags are calt/liga/pnum/tnum with no zero feature. This is a visual ambiguity observation, not a measured reading-error rate.
findings.recommendation: For identifiers, provide a distinguishable zero alternate or avoid relying on O/0 discrimination. Keep the ordinary zero for financial amounts if desired.
findings.acceptance_test: Review randomized O/0 identifiers at 12/14/16px on target rasterizers and validate a distinguishable optional zero with actual shaping.

findings.title: Small data typography needs a weight policy
findings.evidence: Native 12/14/16px proof shows wght 100 markedly faint; 900/opsz 128 is markedly dense at these small sizes. wght 400–500/opsz 9–14 gives visibly more even numeric and currency reading in these samples.
findings.recommendation: Use 400–500 with text optical sizes for dense dashboards; reserve extremes for intentional display treatment.
findings.acceptance_test: Inspect realistic data tables at 12/14/16px and target DPRs, including hover/disabled states, before adopting weight extremes.

positive_evidence: TTF and WOFF2 decoded with fontTools have identical HarfBuzz glyph IDs, advances, and offsets for all 900 sampled shaping cases.
tnum gives equal ten-digit advances at all 20 weight/opsz combinations; full timer and decimal amount widths remain stable.
At wght 400/opsz 14 pnum digit advances are [1268,928,1214,1262,1296,1244,1282,1144,1286,1282] font units.
Default timer widths 00:00:00 / 11:11:11 / 88:88:88 are 8780 / 6740 / 8888 units: explicit tnum is necessary and works.

Punctuation contexts a:a, 1:1, a,a, 1,1, a.a, 1.1, a a, 1 1, a/a, 1/1 were compared under default/tnum/pnum. tnum does not change the tested prose punctuation or space widths. Numeric comma/period kerning is removed with tnum, preserving alignment.
limits: No prior/current reviewer reports were consulted. No font/source changes made.
WOFF2 tested after decoding with fontTools, not browser network loading; no CoreText or DirectWrite validation.
FreeType grayscale rendering at native 12/14/16px plus 28–32px representative numerical proof; no user reading-error study.
Coverage probe also found ₹ ₩ ₴ ₸ ₿ and ≈ absent; relevance depends on intended product languages and markets.
No continuous variable-axis sweep or full glyph-outline/collision audit.
